The inherited adverse known-axis common-earnings case is 10.600906 trillion versus reported common reference 26.457802 trillion. The mix of recoveries, reversal and total-credit-cost proxy changes forward earnings precision materially; this is high economic estimation uncertainty, not a penalty for missing files or a cost-of-equity grid width.
disconfirmingEvidence: Four-year group NPAT, loan and deposit observations are positive, reported CAR is available with its framework, and the source-read adjustments can be reconciled. This is not a claim that reported bank profit is false or that the bank fails a stress test.

Some recoveries may be recurring cash realization of previously impaired assets. Removing them entirely or imposing an industrial cash model would be unjustified; the source alternatives do not define a complete probability distribution.

evidence.rationale: The source-linked operating alternatives vary specific credit/recovery/reversal economics and common incidence. The 10.600906 to 26.457802 trillion known-axis envelope is explicitly conditional, not a confidence interval or forecast.

Recovery contribution changes substantially year-to-year and a separate investment reversal boosts the reported period. These economic operands, not arbitrary valuation discount-rate changes, support the high-uncertainty band.

Future common returns depend on loan/cohort credit cost, recurrence of recoveries and capital/funding conditions. A total-credit-charge proxy is not a loan-only expected-loss model; aggregate loan/deposit/reserve ratios do not resolve that dependency.
